newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ farm input prices rise 0.2 pct in June quarter.
newsitem.headline: NZ farm input prices rise 0.2 pct in June quarter.

text.p: The price level of all farm inputs excluding livestock rose on average by 0.2 percent from the March to the June quarters, Statistics NZ said on Wednesday.
This reversed a fall of 0.2 percent for the previous quarter.
The annual change from the June 1995 quarter was a decrease of 0.1 percent.
SNZ said the main factor behind the June quarter rise was a rise in wages and salaries. A smaller contribution came from higher prices for feed, grazing, cultivation and harvesting.
Partially offsetting price decreases were recorded for repairs and maintenance, and interest rates.
Input prices rose 0.5 percent for cropping and other farms, 0.3 percent for horticultural farms and 0.1 percent for sheep and beef farms and for dairy farms.

For the year to June, there were decreases of 0.3 percent for dairy farms, 0.2 percent for sheep and beef farms and 0.1 percent for horticultural farms. Cropping and other farms showed a 0.9 percent increase.
When livestock was included, there was no change in farm inputs over the quarter but price levels were down by 1.0 percent on average compared with the same quarter last year.

Livestock prices fell by 8.9 percent over the year but were partially offset by price rises in other inputs, especially insurance premiums, and local and central government rates and fees. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
